about: Endgame trainer positions for Chess Lab Open: standard textbook endings, set up by hand. goal: win | draw (for the side to move). end: mate = finish with checkmate; convert = any capture or promotion that keeps the win also counts; hold:N = keep the draw for N of your moves. tools/build_endgames.py checks every goal against the Lichess tablebase.

positions.title: Queen mate
positions.text: Box the king in with the queen a knight's jump away, shrink the box, then bring your king over. Watch for stalemate: never leave the king with no squares when it is not in check.

positions.title: Rook mate
positions.text: Use the rook to cut the king off along a rank or file, bring your king up opposite it, and push the box in one line at a time. A waiting rook move gains the opposition when you need it.

positions.title: Two bishops mate
positions.text: Side by side, the bishops make a wall the king cannot cross. Drive it to the edge, then into a corner, with your king close behind.

positions.title: Bishop and knight mate
positions.text: The hardest basic mate. Mate only works in a corner of your bishop's colour, so first drive the king to the edge, then walk it along the edge into that corner (the knight's W manoeuvre).

positions.title: Bishop and knight: the wrong corner
positions.text: The king sits in the corner your bishop cannot cover. Push it along the edge to the right corner without letting it escape back to the middle.

positions.title: Key squares
positions.text: Your king already stands on a key square in front of the pawn. Keep it in front and the pawn walks home; push the pawn too early and it is a draw.

positions.title: King in front of the pawn
positions.text: Lead with the king, not the pawn. Reach one of the key squares two ranks in front of the pawn and the win is automatic.

positions.title: Opposition: the waiting move
positions.text: The kings face each other. Use the spare pawn move at the right moment to hand the move to Black, so his king has to give way.

positions.title: Hold with the opposition
positions.text: Stay in front of the pawn and take the opposition every time the white king steps up. When the pawn reaches the 7th with check, go straight back, not to the side.

positions.title: Back to the right square
positions.text: Only one square keeps the draw here: answer the white king's approach with the opposition, and retreat straight back, never diagonally away from the pawn.

positions.title: The rook pawn
positions.text: Against a rook pawn, reaching the corner in front of it is enough: the king can never be driven out. Head for a8.

positions.title: The square of the pawn
positions.text: Draw the square from the pawn to its queening square (counting the double step). If your king can step into it, you catch the pawn.

positions.title: Réti's draw
positions.text: It looks hopeless, but a king that walks diagonally chases two goals at once: catching the h-pawn and supporting its own pawn.

positions.title: Outside passed pawn
positions.text: A passed pawn far from the other pawns is a decoy. Use it to drag the enemy king away, then march into the other side.

positions.title: Triangulation
positions.text: Mutual blockade: whoever has to move first loses ground. Keep the opposition and do not let your king be pushed off the pawn.

positions.title: Lucena: building a bridge
positions.text: Cut the black king off by a file, bring your rook to the 4th rank, then walk your king out; the rook blocks the checks (the bridge).

positions.title: Lucena: the checks
positions.text: The same idea from the other side: first push the enemy king one more file away with a check, then build the bridge on the 4th rank.

positions.title: Philidor: third-rank defence
positions.text: Keep your rook on your third rank until the pawn advances to it; then go to the back of the board and check from behind.

positions.title: Vančura position
positions.text: Against an a-pawn with the rook in front of it, attack the pawn from the side (on the f-file here) and check from behind as soon as the white king comes out.

positions.title: King cut off
positions.text: Cut the defending king off from the pawn with your rook along a file, then advance king and pawn together.

positions.title: Rook against pawn
positions.text: The pawn is one step from queening. Find the checks and the right square so the rook can stop it in time.

positions.title: Queen against a centre pawn
positions.text: Check and pin until the king has to stand in front of its own pawn; each time it does, bring your king one step closer.

positions.title: Queen against a bishop pawn
positions.text: With a bishop pawn the defender has a stalemate trick: when the queen blocks, go to the corner and let the queen take the pawn only with stalemate.

positions.title: Queen against rook
positions.text: Philidor's position: a quiet queen move puts Black in zugzwang, and the rook has to leave its king. Win the rook with a fork or a skewer.

positions.title: Queen against rook: the defender's checks
positions.text: Keep your king close to your queen so the rook cannot give endless checks, and push the defending king to the edge.

positions.title: The wrong bishop
positions.text: Bishop and rook pawn cannot win when the queening square is the other colour from the bishop. Stay in the corner, or next to it, and never step out of it.

positions.title: Opposite-coloured bishops
positions.text: Control the square in front of the pawn with your bishop or king; the white bishop can never take it away.

positions.title: Bishop stops the pawns
positions.text: Two connected pawns are fast, but a bishop on their diagonal plus the king in front can hold them.

positions.title: Rook against bishop
positions.text: Run to the corner that is not the colour of your bishop; the rook cannot break it. The other corner loses.

positions.title: Rook against knight
positions.text: Keep the knight next to your king. A knight that wanders off is trapped or lost to a fork.

positions.title: Rook and bishop against rook
positions.text: Theoretically drawn but hard to hold in practice. Stay out of the Philidor mating net: keep your king off the edge where you can.
